title: Add trusted self-hosted recovery validation path
rawUserRequest: The repository-owned self-hosted runner is intended to substitute for the affected GitHub Actions runner during the outage. Use it to execute the exact PR #723 candidate without weakening the final hosted merge or release gates.

declaredIntent.summary: Provide bounded diagnostic feedback during a GitHub-hosted Actions outage while retaining the full hosted compatibility matrix as the only merge and release evidence.

outOfScope: Existing compatibility jobs, push triggers, pull_request triggers, required checks, and compatibility-gate semantics; only a default-off workflow_dispatch recovery_diagnostic input and isolated diagnostic job are in scope
GitHub required-check configuration, branch protection, runner registration, deletion, and service lifecycle; only adding ai-cockpit-recovery to repository runner 21 is in scope
Executing code from pull_request events on a self-hosted runner
Any claim that recovery workflow results are merge or release evidence

acceptance: The existing compatibility workflow exposes a default-off recovery_diagnostic workflow_dispatch input while preserving all push and pull_request matrix behavior.

The recovery_diagnostic job requires the exact labels self-hosted, macOS, X64, and ai-cockpit-recovery, and checks out only PR #723 candidate 365f5e30c9531d8d8948079fe58b8424ecc9efa7 before executing compatibility-test.
The test-weakening guard distinguishes an optional workflow_dispatch input from a required CI check being made nonblocking, while preserving its required-check downgrade signal.
The recovery_diagnostic job runs the repository's macOS-supported compatibility-test command for the immutable PR #723 candidate and publishes an explicit non-release result summary.

A self-hosted diagnostic dispatch for the exact PR #723 candidate commit is prepared and recorded as temporary runner-substitution evidence; it cannot satisfy compatibility, merge, archive, or release gates.
tests/test_workflows.py prevents trigger, label, source-identity, and non-release-boundary regressions.
The committed SBOM is regenerated so its workflow-action coverage includes the additional pinned checkout action.
All candidate release and generated documentation evidence affected by the SBOM refresh is regenerated through the repository's canonical generator chain.

The operations guide names the recovery dispatch command, immutable #723 SHA, four runner labels, compatibility-test command, non-release evidence classification, and the mandatory hosted smoke and compatibility rerun after recovery.
guidelines: Do not execute untrusted fork or pull-request code on a personal self-hosted runner.
Recovery evidence is diagnostic only and cannot satisfy compatibility, merge, or release gates.
Document operational commands and security boundaries with the workflow change.

intent.problem: A GitHub Actions outage prevents PR #723 candidate 365f5e30c9531d8d8948079fe58b8424ecc9efa7 from obtaining runner feedback. A new standalone workflow cannot be manually dispatched until it first exists on the default branch; changing the required hosted matrix, violating the compatibility-versus-smoke quality ownership boundary, or executing arbitrary ref input on a personal runner would weaken evidence or security.
constraints: Use only the existing compatibility workflow's workflow_dispatch surface with a default-off recovery_diagnostic input.
The recovery job never runs for push or pull_request events.
Use an isolated custom recovery label in addition to macOS/X64 self-hosted labels.
Check out and verify only PR #723 candidate 365f5e30c9531d8d8948079fe58b8424ecc9efa7 before executing make compatibility-test.
Do not duplicate smoke.yml's make quality ownership in compatibility.yml.
Do not change existing compatibility jobs, smoke.yml, release.yml, branch protection, or required checks.
Results must remain non-release, non-merge temporary runner-substitution evidence.
intent.rationale: GitHub can dispatch an already-default-branch-registered workflow at the maintenance-branch ref. Binding its isolated job to the exact PR #723 candidate lets the repository-owned runner replace the affected runner during the outage, while the hosted matrix remains the sole authoritative cross-platform gate.
